clues.text: These days were named after the lot that Haman the Agagite cast to crush and destroy the Jews.
In the kingdom of Xerxes, the Jews bound themselves to celebrate these two days at the appointed time every year.
Among the Jews of Persia, every generation, family, province and city was to remember these days so their memory would never fade.
Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wrote with Mordecai and full authority to confirm a second letter about these days.
Mordecai sent letters of peace and truth to the Jews in all 127 provinces of Xerxes to confirm these days.
Mordecai and Queen Esther set times of fasting and lamentation as part of these yearly days for the Jews.
These days recall how Haman's wicked scheme came back on his own head, and he and his sons were hanged.
